researchStatusNote: Scores are EDITORIAL DRAFT ASSESSMENTS written for the MVP. They are not yet cross-checked against the labour-market, salary and automation datasets listed in data/sources.json. Treat every score as an opinion with the stated confidence until a family's status is upgraded after source review. A score of 0 is a real low rating, never missing data.

0.label: MUST NOT
0.meaning: Very poor alignment or a strong reason to avoid under this criterion

4.label: MUST
4.meaning: Very strong alignment; one of the strongest recommendations under this criterion

families.name: Software and Computing
families.description: Programming, software engineering and core computer science.

islamic.rationale: Software is neutral, but employers vary: gambling, interest-lending and surveillance products raise concerns that depend on the specific job.

benefit.rationale: Software underpins health, education, finance and communication systems, though much commercial software has modest social value.

financial.rationale: Entry pay is often good and senior pay strong in many markets; varies widely by country and employer.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand for software capability is expected to remain central to most industries.

aiResilience.rationale: AI coding assistants automate routine coding; system design, debugging at scale and accountability remain human-heavy.

employmentStability.rationale: Demand has been cyclical, with notable layoffs in some downturns.

flexibility.rationale: Skills transfer across industries, countries and remote work.

assumptions: Pay and demand figures are general patterns, not country-specific data.
Islamic alignment depends on the employer and product, not the degree.
changeFactors: Rapid changes in AI coding tools could lower the AI-resilience score.
A local job market that lacks software roles would lower the financial score.

families.name: AI, Machine Learning and Data Science
families.description: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science and analytics.

islamic.rationale: Techniques are neutral; applications in advertising, surveillance or interest-based lending need individual judgement.

benefit.rationale: Useful in medicine, climate, logistics and public services, with a real risk of misuse in surveillance and manipulation.

financial.rationale: Data and AI roles are commonly paid above general technology roles, though many entry roles are modest.

futureResilience.rationale: Data-driven decision-making and AI adoption are widely expected to keep growing.

aiResilience.rationale: Standard modelling and reporting tasks are increasingly automated; problem framing, data quality and validation remain human-led.

employmentStability.rationale: Strong long-run demand, but hiring can fall sharply in some cycles.

flexibility.rationale: Quantitative skills transfer well, but many roles favour postgraduate study or strong portfolios.

assumptions: Degree-level AI and data science programmes are new and their graduates' outcomes are not yet well documented.
changeFactors: Evidence on graduate outcomes from new AI degrees would change the confidence level.
Restrictions on AI deployment could affect demand.

families.name: IT and Information Systems
families.description: IT support, information systems, IT management, and information management.

islamic.rationale: Generally neutral; organisational context determines the concerns, such as gambling or interest-based finance systems.

benefit.rationale: Keeps organisations, hospitals and schools operating; the social value is real but largely indirect.

financial.rationale: Entry pay is often moderate; higher earnings usually need further certification or specialisation.

futureResilience.rationale: Organisations will keep needing information systems, but routine support is changing quickly.

aiResilience.rationale: Help-desk, reporting and routine administration tasks are highly exposed to automation.

employmentStability.rationale: Broadly stable, with demand concentrated in larger employers and in government.

flexibility.rationale: Good transfer to business roles, though some specialist skills are narrower.

assumptions: Routine IT support is the most exposed part of this family; analysis and governance roles are less exposed.
changeFactors: Automation of routine IT administration would lower the AI-resilience score.
Strong local demand for systems roles would raise the financial score.

families.name: Cybersecurity and Information Assurance
families.description: Information security, assurance, and security operations.

islamic.rationale: Protecting data, privacy and trust fits the principle of preventing harm; offensive work needs ethical scrutiny.

benefit.rationale: Protects individuals, hospitals, utilities and public institutions from harm.

financial.rationale: Good demand and pay in many markets; entry-level roles can be competitive.

futureResilience.rationale: Threats and regulation are both growing, which keeps demand durable.

aiResilience.rationale: Monitoring and triage are partly automated, but investigation, response and governance remain human-led.

employmentStability.rationale: Strong demand; hiring can slow in cost-cutting periods.

flexibility.rationale: Certifications transfer across sectors and countries; security clearances can limit some moves.

assumptions: Certifications are often needed for progression; the degree alone may not be sufficient.
changeFactors: Clearance or defence-only work may limit portability.
Changes in threat levels or regulation could shift demand.
families.additionalQualifications: Industry certifications are commonly expected for progression (not verified for each employer).

families.name: Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering
families.description: Power, electronics, embedded systems, communications and computer hardware.

islamic.rationale: Power, water, health and communications systems serve the public; defence-related product lines need individual judgement.

benefit.rationale: Energy, communications and health devices are among the most direct contributions to welfare.

financial.rationale: Solid pay for professional engineers; licensing and experience raise progression.

futureResilience.rationale: Electrification, grids and electronics will remain important, though hardware cycles vary.

aiResilience.rationale: Design and hands-on work are relatively resistant; documentation and simulation tasks are increasingly automated.

employmentStability.rationale: Stable in infrastructure and utilities; more cyclical in consumer electronics.

flexibility.rationale: Professional registration can help abroad, but requirements differ by country.

assumptions: Professional licensing requirements differ by country and are not documented here.
changeFactors: Grid and energy investment levels change demand.
Defence-sector work may raise ethical questions for some students.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional engineering registration may be required for senior work (country-specific).

families.name: Mechanical, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering
families.description: Machines, production systems, process improvement and operations engineering.

islamic.rationale: Makes goods and improves production; concerns depend on what is produced, such as alcohol, tobacco or weapons.

benefit.rationale: Produces goods and improves efficiency; benefit depends on product and sector.

financial.rationale: Good pay in manufacturing hubs; varies by region and sector.

futureResilience.rationale: Advanced manufacturing and automation keep demand, though relocation of production is a risk.

aiResilience.rationale: Physical production and on-site problem-solving are less exposed than desk-based analysis.

employmentStability.rationale: Moderately cyclical; demand follows investment and trade cycles.

flexibility.rationale: Engineering skills transfer to automotive, energy, healthcare devices and consulting.

assumptions: Manufacturing jobs differ greatly in sector; the Islamic-alignment score depends on the product line.
changeFactors: Employer-level choices about products matter more than the degree title.
Automation trends could shift the roles available.

families.name: Civil Engineering and Construction Management
families.description: Infrastructure, structures, water, transport and construction management.

islamic.rationale: Builds housing, water and transport infrastructure; project finance may involve interest-based loans that need case-by-case review.

benefit.rationale: Infrastructure like clean water, roads and shelter directly benefits communities.

financial.rationale: Solid professional pay; construction cycles and public spending affect demand.

futureResilience.rationale: Infrastructure renewal and climate adaptation support demand, though it is cyclical.

aiResilience.rationale: Site work and judgement are resilient; design drafting and cost estimation are increasingly automated.

employmentStability.rationale: Stable in public infrastructure; more cyclical in private construction.

flexibility.rationale: Licensing is largely national; cross-border work requires re-registration.

assumptions: Licensing and registration rules vary by country and are not documented here.
changeFactors: Public investment in infrastructure changes demand.
Climate policy could increase demand for adaptation projects.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional registration is required for independent practice in many countries.

families.name: Architecture and Urban Planning
families.description: Architectural design, building regulation and urban planning.

islamic.rationale: Designing homes, mosques, schools and public space is widely valued; some commissions and ornamentation questions need judgement.

benefit.rationale: Shapes housing, public health and urban life, though many projects are commercial.

financial.rationale: Pay rises with licensure and seniority; early-career pay is often modest.

futureResilience.rationale: Urbanisation and climate adaptation sustain demand for planning expertise.

aiResilience.rationale: Generative design tools are changing drafting; licensed responsibility and client judgement remain human.

employmentStability.rationale: Architecture is cyclical and sensitive to construction slowdowns.

flexibility.rationale: Architectural licensing is national, which limits mobility without re-qualification.

assumptions: Architectural licensure is typically required for the title 'architect'; requirements differ by country.
changeFactors: Licensing reforms in the target country would change flexibility.
Downturns in construction would lower the stability score.
families.additionalQualifications: Licensure and examinations are required for practice (country-specific).

families.name: Chemical and Materials Engineering
families.description: Process engineering, chemical plants, materials science and metallurgy.

islamic.rationale: Many plants serve petrochemical, alcohol, tobacco or industrial food chains; the sector needs careful selection, while pharmaceutical and food roles can be suitable.

benefit.rationale: Materials and process know-how support medicine, energy and infrastructure.

financial.rationale: Solid process-industry pay; some sectors are cyclical.

futureResilience.rationale: Clean energy, batteries and advanced materials create demand, while fossil-based processes decline.

aiResilience.rationale: Plant operations and experimental judgement are fairly resilient; simulation and data tasks are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Commodity-linked demand makes process-industry employment cyclical.

flexibility.rationale: Process and materials skills transfer across sectors.

assumptions: Sector mix within chemical engineering is highly varied; scores are a broad average.
changeFactors: Energy transition policy changes the sector mix.
Employer choices (alcohol, tobacco, petrochemicals) change the Islamic-alignment score.

families.name: Energy, Petroleum, Mining and Nuclear Engineering
families.description: Oil and gas, mining, geological engineering and nuclear energy.

islamic.rationale: Much work is in fossil-fuel extraction or nuclear facilities; scholars differ on whether such work is permissible, so individual judgement and scholarly consultation are needed.

benefit.rationale: Energy supply is essential to welfare; environmental and safety costs are substantial and debated.

financial.rationale: Petroleum and mining roles have often paid well, though pay is cyclical with commodity prices.

futureResilience.rationale: Fossil-fuel demand is expected to decline in many scenarios, though transition and decommissioning skills stay relevant.

aiResilience.rationale: Field and safety-critical work is relatively resilient; modelling tasks are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Commodity booms and busts make employment highly cyclical.

flexibility.rationale: Specialised skills transfer to some sectors, but jobs are often location-specific.

assumptions: Scholarly positions on fossil-fuel and nuclear employment differ; this score describes the sector, not a ruling.
changeFactors: Choice of employer or sub-sector (e.g. renewable or decommissioning work) changes the score.
Commodity prices strongly affect pay and stability.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional registration and sector-specific safety certifications are commonly required.

families.name: Aerospace, Aviation and Aeronautics
families.description: Aircraft and space engineering, aviation operations, maintenance and air traffic management.

islamic.rationale: Civil aviation is broadly neutral, but defence work and airline service of alcohol or gambling-linked activities need individual judgement.

benefit.rationale: Air transport connects people and supports trade, medicine and disaster response.

financial.rationale: Strong pay in some roles (e.g. air traffic control, licensed maintenance); airline pay varies.

futureResilience.rationale: Air travel demand is expected to grow in many regions, with sustainability pressure.

aiResilience.rationale: Safety-critical, licensed, physical roles are relatively resilient; some planning tasks are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Airline employment is cyclical and sensitive to shocks such as pandemics and fuel prices.

flexibility.rationale: Licensed aviation skills can transfer internationally, subject to licensing.

assumptions: Licensing for maintenance and air traffic roles is country-specific and a major barrier.
families.additionalQualifications: Aviation licences or certifications (e.g. maintenance or air-traffic licences) are required for licensed roles.

families.name: Marine, Naval and Ocean Sciences
families.description: Marine engineering, naval architecture and oceanography.

islamic.rationale: Shipping can carry prohibited goods and naval work can be defence-related; ocean science is broadly neutral.

benefit.rationale: Shipping carries most world trade; ocean science informs climate and fisheries.

financial.rationale: Certified seafarers and engineers can earn well; many entry roles involve time at sea.

futureResilience.rationale: Trade and ocean monitoring remain important; decarbonising shipping creates new skills.

aiResilience.rationale: Hands-on engineering and seamanship are resilient; design and monitoring tasks are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Shipping is cyclical; sea-going work may affect family life and stability.

flexibility.rationale: Internationally recognised certificates aid mobility, though licensing is required.

assumptions: Sea-going certification (e.g. STCW-type) requirements are not verified in this build.
families.additionalQualifications: Maritime certification is required for sea-going roles (not verified).

families.name: Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering
families.description: Medical devices, imaging, biomaterials and health technology.

islamic.rationale: Medical devices and diagnostics serve healing; animal testing and some research uses need ethical review.

benefit.rationale: Directly supports diagnosis and treatment of patients.

financial.rationale: Good pay in device companies and hospitals; research pay is often lower early on.

futureResilience.rationale: Ageing populations and health technology sustain demand.

aiResilience.rationale: Regulated, clinical and hands-on work is resilient; design simulation is exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Healthcare-linked demand is comparatively steady.

flexibility.rationale: Skills transfer between devices, hospitals and research; regulatory knowledge varies by country.

assumptions: Bioengineering and biomedical engineering titles overlap substantially in practice.

families.name: Business Administration and General Management
families.description: Business administration, general management, leadership and entrepreneurship.

islamic.rationale: Business ethics are central, but many business roles involve interest-based finance, gambling-linked or alcohol-linked clients; choose the sector carefully.

benefit.rationale: Generalist degrees have indirect social value; the benefit depends strongly on what the business does.

financial.rationale: Wide variation; generalist entry pay is often moderate and senior pay depends on specialisation.

futureResilience.rationale: General management skills persist, but generalist degrees are less distinctive in an automated market.

aiResilience.rationale: Routine reporting and administration are exposed; judgement, negotiation and leadership are less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Generalist roles are easier to cut in downturns.

flexibility.rationale: Generalist skills move across sectors and can support self-employment.

assumptions: Generalist business degrees vary widely in quality between institutions; the specialisation matters more.
changeFactors: Choice of specialisation (e.g. analytics, operations) would raise several scores.
Entrepreneurship ability and access to capital.

families.name: Project, Operations and Engineering Management
families.description: Project management, facility management, operations and engineering management.

islamic.rationale: Coordinating public, health and infrastructure projects can be highly beneficial; the sector served determines the score.

benefit.rationale: Delivers projects and services that others depend on.

financial.rationale: Good pay in project-heavy sectors, especially with certification.

futureResilience.rationale: Project-based work continues across industries; methods are changing.

aiResilience.rationale: Planning software automates scheduling; stakeholder management and risk judgement remain human.

employmentStability.rationale: Demand is broad but tied to project pipelines.

flexibility.rationale: Project and operations skills transfer across sectors and countries.

assumptions: Certifications such as PMP-type credentials are common but cost money and require experience.
changeFactors: Experience requirements in the target market.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional project-management certification is commonly sought after work experience (not verified per employer).

families.name: Marketing, Advertising and Sales
families.description: Marketing, advertising, sales management and brand strategy.

islamic.rationale: Promotion of alcohol, gambling, interest-based products or manipulative sales raises concerns; halal and ethical brands exist but are a narrower market.

benefit.rationale: Helps businesses find customers; social value is mixed and depends on the product being sold.

financial.rationale: Pay varies; senior commercial roles can be well paid.

futureResilience.rationale: Digital channels and AI content tools are changing the field quickly.

aiResilience.rationale: Content creation, copywriting, reporting and campaign optimisation are highly exposed to AI tools.

employmentStability.rationale: Marketing budgets are cut early in downturns.

flexibility.rationale: Commercial and communication skills transfer across sectors.

assumptions: Advertising and sales roles differ in ethical exposure from employer to employer.
changeFactors: Choice of industry (e.g. halal food, education, health) would change the Islamic-alignment score.

families.name: Communications, Journalism and Public Relations
families.description: Communications, journalism, public relations and media studies.

islamic.rationale: Truthful reporting and public information are valued; media employers vary, and some content conflicts with Islamic values.

benefit.rationale: Accurate public information supports accountability and informed citizens.

financial.rationale: Many media and journalism roles pay modestly and have shrinking traditional employment.

futureResilience.rationale: Traditional print and broadcast contract; digital and communications roles are growing but competitive.

aiResilience.rationale: Routine writing, summarising and content production are highly exposed to generative AI.

employmentStability.rationale: Media employment has been unstable and cyclical.

flexibility.rationale: Writing, research and communication skills transfer to many sectors.

assumptions: Public relations is generally more stable than newsroom journalism, but the evidence is not verified here.
changeFactors: Employer choice (public service or nonprofit media vs entertainment).

families.name: Design, Studio Art and Photography
families.description: Studio art, graphic design and photography.

islamic.rationale: Creative work is valued, but depictions of living beings and some commercial content are matters of scholarly disagreement and personal judgement.

benefit.rationale: Creative work has cultural and communicative value; direct welfare benefit varies.

financial.rationale: Most creative careers are freelance and income is irregular.

futureResilience.rationale: Image and design tools are changing; demand for original creative judgement persists.

aiResilience.rationale: Generative image tools substitute for many routine design and stock tasks.

employmentStability.rationale: Freelance and project-based income makes stability low.

flexibility.rationale: Portfolio work travels well and supports self-employment.

assumptions: Scholarly positions on depicting living beings differ; this score does not rule on them.
changeFactors: Specialism within design (e.g. product, architecture visualisation, Islamic-compliant design).

families.name: Biological Sciences, Molecular Biology and Biotechnology
families.description: Biology, zoology, molecular biology and biotechnology.

islamic.rationale: Studying life and nature supports reflection on creation; some research (animal testing, genetic modification) needs ethical review.

benefit.rationale: Supports medicine, agriculture and environmental work; many entry roles are lab-based.

financial.rationale: Bachelor-level pay is modest; higher pay usually follows postgraduate study.

futureResilience.rationale: Biotechnology and life-science research are expected to keep expanding.

aiResilience.rationale: Data analysis is exposed; wet-lab skill and experimental judgement are less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Research funding cycles make some roles insecure.

flexibility.rationale: Lab and analytical skills transfer across health, food and environment sectors.

assumptions: Postgraduate study is typically needed for research careers.
families.additionalQualifications: Postgraduate study is commonly needed for research and higher pay.

families.name: Physics and Chemistry
families.description: Physics and chemistry, including applied and theoretical streams.

islamic.rationale: Study of the natural world is widely valued; some applications (weapons, chemical agents) need ethical judgement.

benefit.rationale: Underpins technology, energy and medicine, although bachelor-level impact is indirect.

financial.rationale: Bachelor-level pay is modest; higher pay usually needs postgraduate study or industry experience.

futureResilience.rationale: Core science remains important; specific applications change.

aiResilience.rationale: Computational and analytical tasks are exposed; experimental and theoretical judgement is less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Research and teaching jobs can be limited and funding-dependent.

flexibility.rationale: Quantitative and analytical skills transfer very widely.

assumptions: Pay and demand are general patterns and depend on postgraduate study.
families.additionalQualifications: Postgraduate study is commonly needed for research careers.

families.name: Geology, Geoscience and Meteorology
families.description: Earth sciences, geology, geoscience and atmospheric science.

islamic.rationale: Geology often serves extractive industries; groundwater, climate and hazard work is widely beneficial.

benefit.rationale: Water, hazard and climate work is valuable; extraction work has mixed impact.

financial.rationale: Good pay in resource sectors; environmental and water roles are steadier but lower-paid.

futureResilience.rationale: Climate and water issues sustain demand; resource-sector demand is cyclical.

aiResilience.rationale: Field observation is resilient; forecasting and data modelling are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Resource-linked employment is cyclical; government and consulting roles are steadier.

flexibility.rationale: Fieldwork skills and GIS transfer, though some roles are location-bound.

assumptions: Degree-level geology jobs are often field or resource-sector roles; professional registration may be required in some countries.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional registration may be required (country-specific).

families.name: Mathematics and Statistics
families.description: Pure and applied mathematics, statistics and quantitative reasoning.

islamic.rationale: Mathematics is valued across traditions; the applications determine any concerns.

benefit.rationale: Supports medicine, public health, economics and engineering through quantitative methods.

financial.rationale: Strong pay in quantitative roles, particularly with further training.

futureResilience.rationale: Quantitative reasoning underpins most data-driven fields.

aiResilience.rationale: Routine calculation and modelling are exposed; proof, problem framing and rigorous inference are less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Broad demand across sectors; statistical roles in government are steady.

flexibility.rationale: Highly transferable across industries and countries.

assumptions: Actuarial professional exams are separate from the degree.
families.additionalQualifications: Actuarial or statistical professional exams may be needed for specialist roles.

families.name: Accounting and Auditing
families.description: Financial accounting, auditing, taxation and management accounting.

islamic.rationale: Accounting is broadly neutral, but clients may be interest-based or prohibited-sector businesses; Islamic finance and zakat-related accounting are valid specialisms.

benefit.rationale: Accurate records and audits support honest markets and public trust.

financial.rationale: Professional accounting qualifications are commonly well paid and progressive.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand persists for assurance and regulatory compliance; routine bookkeeping is shrinking.

aiResilience.rationale: Bookkeeping and data entry are highly exposed; judgement, assurance and tax advice remain human-led.

employmentStability.rationale: Accounting work is comparatively steady across economic cycles.

flexibility.rationale: Professional qualifications transfer across sectors and, in some systems, internationally.

assumptions: Professional accounting exams are a major investment beyond the degree.
changeFactors: Professional body membership and exam costs.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional accounting qualification (e.g. ACCA, CA, CPA-type) is usually needed for senior roles.

families.name: Finance, Economics and Actuarial Science
families.description: Corporate finance, banking, economics, investment and actuarial science.

islamic.rationale: Conventional banking, lending, insurance and investment rely heavily on interest and uncertainty; Islamic finance is a real alternative, but most finance roles need careful selection.

benefit.rationale: Benefit depends on the institution; well-run finance supports growth, while speculative finance can harm.

financial.rationale: Finance roles are often among the higher-paid bachelor-level paths, especially in investment and actuarial work.

futureResilience.rationale: Routine analysis and some trading roles are being automated; advisory and risk roles are more durable.

aiResilience.rationale: Modelling and reporting are exposed; client relationships and regulated judgement are less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Stable in regulated institutions; cyclical in investment markets.

flexibility.rationale: Quantitative and finance skills transfer, though some roles need further qualifications.

assumptions: Riba concerns apply to the interest-based products and contracts that a role involves; scholarly views differ on specific roles.
changeFactors: Choosing Islamic finance, ethical investment or non-interest-based roles would change the Islamic score.
families.additionalQualifications: Actuarial and investment professional exams are needed for specialist roles.

families.name: Human Resources and Personnel Management
families.description: Recruitment, employee relations, training and workforce planning.

islamic.rationale: Fair treatment, consultation and care for workers fit well with Islamic principles of justice in employment.

benefit.rationale: Improves organisations' treatment of staff and the quality of work.

financial.rationale: Entry pay is modest; senior HR leadership pays well but is competitive.

futureResilience.rationale: People management stays necessary, though some administration is automated.

aiResilience.rationale: Screening, scheduling and records are increasingly automated; employee relations and judgement remain human.

employmentStability.rationale: Broad demand across organisations.

flexibility.rationale: Transfers across sectors; specialist certifications help.

assumptions: Pay and demand vary greatly by country.
changeFactors: Employer sector (e.g. recruitment for prohibited industries).
families.additionalQualifications: Professional HR certification is commonly sought.

families.name: Agriculture and Food Science
families.description: Crop and animal production, agronomy, food science, and food safety.

islamic.rationale: Growing food and supporting farmers is widely valued; animal husbandry and halal food processing require attention to standards.

benefit.rationale: Food security and farmer livelihoods are central to welfare.

financial.rationale: Pay is modest in many agricultural roles, with higher pay in agribusiness and food-tech.

futureResilience.rationale: Food demand and climate adaptation sustain need; technology is changing practice.

aiResilience.rationale: Field and animal work is resilient; precision-agriculture analytics are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Food systems are relatively steady; agricultural income is weather-dependent.

flexibility.rationale: Local knowledge and agro-ecological conditions limit portability.

assumptions: Pakistan-specific agricultural labour market data are not yet extracted.

families.name: Environmental Science, Engineering and Sustainability
families.description: Environmental science, environmental engineering, sustainability and environmental health and safety.

islamic.rationale: Protecting the environment and preventing harm connects with stewardship principles; interpretation is conceptual rather than a ruling.

benefit.rationale: Directly protects air, water and health.

financial.rationale: Pay ranges from modest to good; public-sector and NGO work is often lower paid.

futureResilience.rationale: Environmental regulation and climate adaptation are expanding areas.

aiResilience.rationale: Field inspection, regulation and on-site engineering are resilient; reporting and modelling are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Regulation-driven demand is relatively steady.

flexibility.rationale: Transferable across sectors; professional registration varies by country.

assumptions: Environmental careers may involve regulation of extractive industries; this is a sector-level note.
changeFactors: Regulatory strength in the target country.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional registration may be needed for engineering roles.

families.name: Health Administration and Public Health
families.description: Health services management, hospital administration, health management and public health administration.

islamic.rationale: Organising care and preventing disease is widely regarded as beneficial.

benefit.rationale: Directly improves access to care and population health.

financial.rationale: Good pay for senior health managers; entry roles are moderate.

futureResilience.rationale: Ageing, chronic disease and health-system demand keep this field important.

aiResilience.rationale: Management and policy judgement remain human; administrative and reporting work is exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Healthcare-linked demand is steady.

flexibility.rationale: Skills transfer across health systems, though systems differ by country.

assumptions: Degree titles vary; some health administration programmes are postgraduate in certain countries.
changeFactors: Whether a programme is accredited locally.

families.name: Nursing
families.description: Registered nursing and clinical nursing care.

islamic.rationale: Caring for the sick is widely valued; privacy and modesty considerations can be managed in many settings.

benefit.rationale: Direct patient care with high social value.

financial.rationale: Pay varies greatly by country; experienced nurses in high-income markets earn well.

futureResilience.rationale: Ageing populations keep demand for nursing high.

aiResilience.rationale: Hands-on bedside care is resilient; documentation and triage support are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Demand is usually steady, though working conditions can be demanding.

flexibility.rationale: Licensing is national; some nurses migrate after separate registration exams.

assumptions: Licensure and exams are country-specific; the Pakistan Nursing Council requirements are not verified in this build.
families.additionalQualifications: National nursing registration is required to practise (country-specific).

families.name: Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
families.description: Clinical and community pharmacy, drug development and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

islamic.rationale: Clinical pharmacy serves healing; some products may contain alcohol or animal-derived ingredients, so halal sourcing and dispensing need checking.

benefit.rationale: Medicines and medicine safety are directly beneficial.

financial.rationale: Solid pay for licensed pharmacists; research and industry roles vary.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand for medicines grows, though pharmacy roles are changing.

aiResilience.rationale: Dispensing automation is growing; clinical counselling remains human.

employmentStability.rationale: Steady demand; some community pharmacy chains have restructured.

flexibility.rationale: Licensing limits mobility; industry and regulatory roles are more portable.

assumptions: Pharmacist licensure is needed for dispensing; the Pakistan Pharmacy Council requirements are not verified here.
families.additionalQualifications: Pharmacist licensure is needed for dispensing roles (country-specific).

families.name: Medicine (MBBS and equivalent)
families.description: Medical training leading to clinical practice. In some systems (e.g. the United States) this is postgraduate; in Pakistan and several other systems it is an undergraduate degree.

islamic.rationale: Healing the sick is widely regarded as beneficial; some procedures and research raise ethical questions that require case-by-case scholarly guidance.

benefit.rationale: Direct improvement of health and survival.

financial.rationale: Physicians are often among the best-paid professionals, though pay and training costs vary by country.

futureResilience.rationale: Health needs are growing and cannot easily be automated end to end.

aiResilience.rationale: Clinical judgement and procedures are resilient; diagnostic imaging and documentation are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Strong and steady demand; postgraduate training can be long and competitive.

flexibility.rationale: Licensing is national; medical registration exams differ, though international mobility exists.

assumptions: Total training length, cost and licensing are not verified for any country in this build.
changeFactors: Licensing exam requirements in the target country.
families.additionalQualifications: Medical registration and postgraduate training are required for practice (country-specific).

families.name: Education and Teaching
families.description: Teacher training, primary and secondary education, and educational administration.

islamic.rationale: Teaching and knowledge-sharing are highly valued; content and institutional values vary.

benefit.rationale: Shapes learning and opportunity for children and young people.

financial.rationale: Teacher pay is often modest relative to qualifications, varying by country.

futureResilience.rationale: Education remains essential; teaching methods are changing.

aiResilience.rationale: Classroom relationships and supervision are resilient; lesson planning and marking support are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Teaching demand is usually steady, with public-sector stability in many countries.

flexibility.rationale: Teacher registration is often national and language-specific.

assumptions: Teacher registration requirements are country-specific.
families.additionalQualifications: Teaching certification or registration is usually required.

families.name: Public Administration and Nonprofit Management
families.description: Public administration, nonprofit management, fundraising and community development.

islamic.rationale: Public service and charitable work are strongly aligned with Islamic values of service and care; fundraising must be transparent.

benefit.rationale: Directly designed to serve communities.

financial.rationale: Pay is often modest, particularly in nonprofits; civil service pay varies.

futureResilience.rationale: Public and social needs continue; funding models are changing.

aiResilience.rationale: Community trust and relationship work are resilient; reporting and grant-writing support are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Civil service is stable; nonprofit funding can be short-term.

flexibility.rationale: Transferable across public, nonprofit and development sectors.

assumptions: Donor and funding rules for nonprofits differ by country.

families.name: Law and Legal Studies
families.description: Law degrees (LLB) and legal studies, leading to advocacy, legal practice and policy work.

islamic.rationale: Justice and the rule of law are valued, but legal practice can involve interest-based contracts, prohibited-sector clients and adversarial work; ethical choice matters.

benefit.rationale: Access to justice and protection of rights are strong public goods.

financial.rationale: Strong pay in commercial law; public-interest and junior roles pay less.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand for legal services persists; legal technology is changing routine work.

aiResilience.rationale: Legal research and document drafting are highly exposed; advocacy, negotiation and court work are less so.

employmentStability.rationale: Steady demand across legal sectors; junior-level hiring can be competitive.

flexibility.rationale: Legal practice is jurisdiction-specific; the LLB alone may not qualify a graduate to practise.

assumptions: Qualification to practise requires further professional training in most jurisdictions.
changeFactors: Practice area (e.g. human rights, family, commercial).
Professional licensing in the target country.
families.additionalQualifications: Bar or professional training is required to practise in most jurisdictions.

families.name: Psychology and Counselling
families.description: Psychology, counselling and mental-health related work.

islamic.rationale: Supporting mental wellbeing is valued; some therapy approaches may conflict with specific religious views and need careful choice.

benefit.rationale: Direct wellbeing benefit for individuals and families.

financial.rationale: Bachelor-level pay is modest; clinical practice usually needs postgraduate training.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand for mental-health services is growing, though funding is uneven.

aiResilience.rationale: Therapeutic relationships are resilient; some screening and information tasks are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Entry roles are often short-term or low-paid.

flexibility.rationale: Human-services and HR skills transfer.

assumptions: Clinical psychology and counselling usually require postgraduate training and registration.
families.additionalQualifications: Postgraduate training and registration are usually required for clinical practice.

families.name: Political Science, International Relations, Sociology and Social Work
families.description: Political science, international relations, sociology and social work.

islamic.rationale: Social justice, welfare and civic service are strongly aligned; politics and foreign policy involve contested values.

benefit.rationale: Informs policy and supports vulnerable people; impact depends on the role.

financial.rationale: Bachelor-level pay is modest; diplomatic and policy careers often need postgraduate study.

futureResilience.rationale: Governance and social needs persist.

aiResilience.rationale: Human relationships and judgement remain central; research synthesis is exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Government and nonprofit funding can change quickly.

flexibility.rationale: Writing, analysis and cross-cultural skills transfer broadly.

assumptions: Careers in diplomacy are competitive and often require postgraduate study.
changeFactors: Specialisation (e.g. social work with registration) and funding environments.
families.additionalQualifications: Social work registration and postgraduate degrees are often required for specialist roles.

families.name: Islamic Studies and Religious Sciences
families.description: Islamic studies, Qur'anic studies, hadith, fiqh and related religious and humanities studies.

islamic.rationale: Directly engages the religious sciences. Study does not by itself confer authority to issue rulings; that requires qualified scholarly training.

benefit.rationale: Supports education, community service and inter-faith understanding.

financial.rationale: Career market is narrow and pay is often modest unless combined with other qualifications.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand is concentrated in education and religious institutions with limited growth.

aiResilience.rationale: Teaching and community leadership are resilient; text retrieval and translation are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Employment depends on institutions and funding.

flexibility.rationale: Strong in Muslim-majority and academic contexts; transfer to other sectors needs added skills.

assumptions: This family is scored for career fit only; it does not evaluate religious content or scholarly rulings.
changeFactors: Combination with economics, law, IT or teaching qualifications.
families.additionalQualifications: Postgraduate study or specialised scholarly training is usually needed for research and religious-authority roles.

families.name: Hospitality and Tourism Management
families.description: Hotel, restaurant, travel and tourism management.

islamic.rationale: Hospitality often includes alcohol, gambling-linked entertainment and environments hostile to modest conduct; halal and family-focused tourism are alternatives.

benefit.rationale: Provides jobs and cultural exchange; welfare benefit is more modest.

financial.rationale: Pay is often modest with irregular hours; senior roles are better paid.

futureResilience.rationale: Tourism is sensitive to shocks and is changing with digital booking.

aiResilience.rationale: Booking and routine service are exposed; guest relations and event delivery remain human-led.

employmentStability.rationale: Highly seasonal and sensitive to shocks such as pandemics.

flexibility.rationale: Hospitality skills transfer across countries and sectors.

assumptions: Halal tourism is a growing niche whose size is not verified here.

families.name: Sports Science and Recreation
families.description: Exercise and sports science, coaching, physical education and recreation management.

islamic.rationale: Physical health and sport are valued; gambling-linked sports betting, revealing dress and some entertainment settings need individual judgement.

benefit.rationale: Supports physical health and community activity.

financial.rationale: Pay is modest for most entry roles; elite sport is highly competitive.

futureResilience.rationale: Demand for fitness and health promotion persists; elite sport is volatile.

aiResilience.rationale: Coaching and physical instruction are resilient; analytics and programme administration are exposed.

employmentStability.rationale: Many roles are part-time or contract-based.

flexibility.rationale: Coaching and health skills transfer; certification is often needed.

assumptions: Sports scholarships are a separate funding route and are not assessed here.
changeFactors: Public health investment in physical activity.
families.additionalQualifications: Coaching or fitness certifications are commonly needed.

families.name: Languages, Literature and Linguistics
families.description: English and other language studies, literature, linguistics and translation.

islamic.rationale: Language and literature support communication, learning and cross-cultural understanding; content choices matter.

benefit.rationale: Supports education, translation and cross-cultural access to knowledge.

financial.rationale: Pay is modest for many roles; specialist translation and localisation can pay better.

futureResilience.rationale: Machine translation and generative AI are changing translation and writing work quickly.

aiResilience.rationale: Routine translation, copywriting and editing are highly exposed to AI tools.

employmentStability.rationale: Freelance and contract work is common.

flexibility.rationale: Language skills are portable and useful across many sectors.

assumptions: Language skills can be combined with another discipline to improve prospects.
changeFactors: Specialism such as legal or medical translation.
families.additionalQualifications: Translation certification is commonly needed for professional interpreting roles.

families.name: Logistics and Supply Chain Management
families.description: Supply chain, logistics, procurement and transport operations.

islamic.rationale: Moving goods is neutral, but supply chains can carry alcohol, weapons or other prohibited goods; choose sectors carefully.

benefit.rationale: Moves food, medicine and goods; efficiency supports affordability.

financial.rationale: Solid pay in procurement and planning, particularly with certification.

futureResilience.rationale: Global trade and e-commerce keep demand; automation of warehousing is growing.

aiResilience.rationale: Planning software automates forecasting; relationships, exception handling and negotiation remain human.

employmentStability.rationale: Stable core demand, though trade shocks create volatility.

flexibility.rationale: Skills transfer across industries and countries.

assumptions: Professional certifications (e.g. CIPS-type) are valuable but not essential.
families.additionalQualifications: Professional supply-chain certification is commonly sought.
